scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5121: HELP!! My computer (PC1 in Office A) and my
neighbour's (PC2, literally the next desk) have STOPPED SPEAKING to each
other -- yesterday I was pulling files off it fine, today nothing on it
answers me at all. The switch our desks plug into has obviously died (or
PC2's port on it has) -- there is nothing else between two desks!! Please
restart the office switch, or turn PC2's port back on, and make our computers
talk again -- we have a handover due!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC1 and PC2 are both in Office A VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other
  directly over the access switch with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the intra-office L2
  path -- does the agent verify PC1<->PC2 reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate an access-switch/port fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC1 cannot reach
its neighbor PC2 on the same VLAN -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100)
reaches PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss. Both hosts sit in Office A VLAN10 on
the 10.1.0.0/24 subnet and are bridged by the access switch; the traffic stays
local (same subnet, no routing or gateway involved) and the L2 forwarding path
between the two ports is intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-office path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC1->PC2 on the live lab, confirms both hosts are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and that
ARP/L2 forwarding works on the access switch, finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a downed access-switch
port, a VLAN10 misconfiguration, or DSWA1 to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network between PC1 and PC2 is fully operational. A live ping from PC1
(10.1.0.100/24) to PC2 (10.1.0.101/24) returns 4/4 packets with 0% loss and
approximately 1 ms round-trip time, confirming end-to-end Layer-2 reachability.
Inspection of both access switches—aswa2 (where PC1's link_a2_pc segment
terminates) and aswa3 (where PC2's CD_CLIENT_A3 segment terminates)—shows
every relevant port in the Spanning Tree forwarding state: the host-facing
ports (eth0) and the primary uplinks to distribution switch dswa1 (eth1) are
both forwarding. The secondary uplinks to dswa2 (eth2 on each switch) are
correctly blocked by STP to prevent a bridging loop, which is normal and
expected behavior, not a fault.

The user's assertion that "the switch our desks plug into has obviously died"
is factually incorrect on two counts: (1) PC1 and PC2 are not on the same
access switch—PC1 connects via aswa2 and PC2 via aswa3, separated by the
dswa1 distribution switch, and (2) none of those devices exhibit any fault.
The root cause of the ticket is a false premise: the user misidentified
their topology and reported a connectivity failure that does not exist at the
network layer. No corrective action is required on the infrastructure; the
user should verify their application-layer service (e.g., file-sharing daemon,
firewall rules on the PC) if they still cannot transfer files, as the
underlying network path is healthy.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The agent confirmed connectivity but explicitly says the hosts are on different access switches via the distribution switch instead of noting both are up on VLAN10 and directly bridged on the same access switch at baseline.

The investigation log shows successful PC1→PC2 pings and STP/bridge output from both access switches, supporting the agent's conclusion that the L2 path is healthy; one minor mapping (explicit host-to-port association) is implied but not fully printed. Overall the reasoning is sound and covers the necessary checks to dismiss the ticket as a false premise.
